title: CVE-2026-58704: Google Pixel Modem Zero-Day Exploited in Targeted Attacks
content_md: Google has released security updates for a high-severity zero-day vulnerability affecting the cellular modem in Pixel devices after finding signs that the flaw is being used in limited, targeted attacks. Tracked as CVE-2026-58704 and scored 8.0 under CVSS 3.1, the issue can allow an attacker to bypass permission checks and escalate privileges without requiring any interaction from the device owner. The vulnerability results from a logic error in the cellular modem that causes improper authorization. Google’s CVE description says exploitation can lead to remote, proximal or adjacent privilege escalation with no additional execution privileges needed, and the attack does not require the victim to tap a link, open a document, or approve a prompt. That zero-click characteristic significantly raises the operational risk. Unlike common mobile attacks that depend on social engineering, a modem-level vulnerability may potentially be triggered through communications processed below the normal application layer, reducing the opportunities for users to recognize or stop an attack before exploitation occurs. Google has not publicly described the delivery mechanism used in the observed campaign. The September 2026 Pixel update fixes the vulnerability with security patch level 2026-09-05 or later.
